title: I Let the Moving Company Keep the Stair-Fee Photo They Took

parts.text: I watched the mover photograph my stairs to add a fee I had already disclosed. I am twenty-two, first apartment, broke, tape on my fingers. The quote, signed, included two flights. The crew lead, Bo, smiled at his phone. The stairwell smelled like someone else's curry, not mine yet. My friend Asha held the elevator, which was broken, which we had also disclosed. Bo said, "This is extra flights" I said, "Your quote says two. There are two" Bo said surprise stairs. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: His photo is going to billing, and the signed quote already has two flights in bold.

parts.text: I emailed the quote to billing with his photo attached, subject: already priced. Billing, a person named Nia, called Bo off the stairs. The fee vanished. They still dinged a box corner. I photographed that too, because I had learned. Asha bought pizza that tasted like the box. I sat on the floor and loved the floor. Bo said I was difficult. Difficult is a two-flight PDF. The curry neighbors later became friends. The elevator stayed broken for a week, a character in the story. Nia said, "Why is there a stair surcharge" Bo said, "It looked like three" I tipped the two movers who had not held the camera. Not Bo.
